subject: history_social
passage: That Inca administrators used khipus, arrangements of knotted cords, to record numbers is not in dispute: the position and type of each knot correspond to a decimal system, and many khipus tally census figures or goods owed to the state. Whether some khipus also recorded language is a harder question. Spanish chroniclers of the sixteenth century reported that khipu keepers could "read" histories and family lines from the cords, yet such testimony, offered by observers who could not themselves interpret the cords, establishes only that keepers recited narratives while handling khipus, not that the narratives were encoded in them. A few surviving khipus whose cords vary in color and fiber far more than any numerical purpose would require have therefore drawn particular attention.
stem: Based on the text, why have certain surviving khipus drawn particular attention?

choices.A: Their variety of colors and fibers seems to exceed what recording numbers alone would require.
choices.B: They confirm chroniclers' reports that khipu keepers could read histories directly from cords.
choices.C: Their knots, unlike those of the census khipus, do not follow a decimal system of positions.
choices.D: Spanish observers saw keepers reciting narratives while handling these particular khipus.

explanation.why: The text says the chroniclers' reports cannot settle whether khipus recorded language. The last sentence, linked by "therefore," explains why some khipus stand out: their cords vary "far more than any numerical purpose would require." That extra variety is what makes them possible evidence of a non-numerical record.
explanation.A: Correct. This restates the final sentence: the variety goes beyond "any numerical purpose," which is why these khipus interest researchers asking whether khipus recorded language.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text calls the question of language open and says the reports prove less than they seem to; nothing confirms them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text never says these khipus' knots break from the decimal system; it points to color and fiber instead.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text discusses the chroniclers' testimony in general, not observations tied to these particular khipus.
